<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par112"/>{{GHGmargin-letter|112|y}}
Rem. 1. Very frequently the announcement of a future event is attached by means of {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}<ref>On the various combinations with {{GHGheb|text=וָהָיָה}} see König’s statistics in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} xix. 272 ff.</ref> ''and it shall come to pass'' (cf. the analogous continuation in the past by means of {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}}, § 111, 2), after which the event announced (sometimes after a long parenthesis) follows in one or more (co-ordinate) perfects consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=12|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה כִי}}=''if'', as in 46:33, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=26|hidebook=1}} and frequently), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=3}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=9}}; or in the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, 21 ff. (cf. 29:8); or in the jussive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=9}}. It very rarely happens that the verb which is thus loosely added, agrees in gender and number with the following subject, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהָֽיְתָה}} (before {{GHGheb|text=הַחֶ֫רֶב}}), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיִהְיוּ}} (before {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽאֲנָשִׁים}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|z}}
2. The jussive form {{GHGheb|text=וִיהִי}} occurs (in the sense described in ''y'') instead of {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=24}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=14|verse=15}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=4}}, although in the first three places a jussive is wholly inadmissible in the context, and even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=4}} (where an admonition follows) {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} would be expected (see below, bb). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=5}} the form is a textual error, and the pointing should simply be {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}}. In the other passages {{GHGheb|text=ויהי}} (always before an infinitive with a preposition) stands at the beginning of the sentence at an unusually long distance from the principal tone, and hence is certainly to be explained according to {{GHGpar|109|k}}, except that in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=5}}, &c., the simply rhythmical jussive form takes the place, not of the full imperfect form, but (exceptionally) of the perfect consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|aa}}
(''b'') To introduce a command or wish: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=19}} ''love ye therefore the stranger''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=6}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=14}} the precative perfect consecutive, as elsewhere the cohortative, jussive, and imperative, is strengthened by means of {{GHGheb|text=נָא}}). So, also, in loose connexion with participial and other noun-clauses (see above, x), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=12}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=2}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=3}} f., 3:9.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=11}} the perfect consecutive ({{GHGheb|text=וּנְמַלְתֶּם|translate=and ye shall be circumcised}}, &c.) is used to explain a preceding command.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|bb}}
Rem. As in the cases mentioned above under ''y'', the connexion may be made by means of {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}. Thus with a following perfect consecutive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}. Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=14}}, where the real wish, at least as regards the sense, is contained in the next sentence.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|cc}}
(''c'') To introduce a question, whether in loose connexion with another interrogative sentence (see above, p), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=15}} ''art thou my brother'' (equivalent to, ''Surely thou art''), {{GHGheb|text=וַֽעֲבַדְתַּ֫נִי|translate=and shouldest thou then serve me for naught}}? or with a positive statement, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם|translate=will ye then make them rest?}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=11}}, and (if it is {{GHGterm|Mil<sup>e</sup>raʿ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=21}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽהֱרַשְׁתִּי}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|dd}}
(''d'') To introduce actions frequently repeated hence analogous to the numerous examples of a frequentative perfect consecutive, above, under ''e''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְעָלָה}} of annual festival journeys); 13:21 (where, however, the text appears radically corrupt); 27:9 ({{GHGheb|text=וְהִכָּה}}, i.e. every time, therefore continued by means of {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא יְחַיֶּה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְכִלְכְּלוּ}},<section end="par112"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
